02.
1.

This is an application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. in connection with Talcher P.S. Case No.425 of 2023 arising out of C.T. Special (POCSO) Case No.54 of 2023, pending in the Court of the learned Addl. Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Angul under Sections 450, 366, 368,
376 (3), 387, 323, 294, 506, 34 of IPC read with Section 4 (2)/6 (1)/17 of the POCSO Act and Section 9/11 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act.
2. The prayer of the petitioner had been rejected by the learned A.D.J.-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Angul vide order dated 16.08.2023.

3. The prosecution allegation in brief is that on 15.07.2023 at about 10.00 a.m. the complainant-victim lodged a written report before Talcher Police Station that on 21.06.2023 evening, the petitioner forcibly took her to his house and kept physical relationship with her without her consent.
He thereafter married her in Mangala Temple in presence of village gentries.
But the mother of the petitioner, sister, Kasturi Naik and aunt-Mini Naik tortured her by demanding dowry and abused her in obscene language and assaulted her.
On 07.07.2023, the family members of the petitioner demanded one lakh dowry, TV, gold ornaments and tortured her physically and mentally and threw her out from house.

sentences.text:
Opposite Parties on 14 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4806879/
1 present in Court today.
They are duly identified by Mr.A.P.Das, learned Addl. Standing Counsel.
They have filed copies of the Aadhar cards in Court, which are taken on record.
5. Mr. Arijeet Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that two FIR had been lodged against the petitioner in different police station, to harass him.
In this case false allegations have been made due to misunderstanding.
He further submits that the dispute between the parties has been settled and the petitioner and his parents are willing to accept the victim as his wife.
Investigation in the case is over and charge sheet dated 12.09.2023 has been filed.

Petitioner is in custody since 20.07.2023, so he may be released on bail, so that he can bring back the petitioner to his house.
6.
Mr. A.P. Das, learned Addl.
Standing Counsel opposes the prayer for bail stating that the offence is heinous in nature and if the petitioner is released on bail, he will influence prosecution witnesses.
He further submits that chargesheet dated 12.09.2023 has been filed against 14 persons, keeping the investigation open.
The victim is a minor.

7. Mr. Sankar Naik, the opposite party No.2 and his wife who are present in Court submit that they have no objection if the petitioner is released on bail as he has assured to accept the victim as his wife after he is released on bail.

8. Considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the submission of the opposite party No.2 and his wife and the victim, I am inclined to release the petitioner on interim bail for a period of six months.

9. Let the petitioner- Prem @ Premananda Naik be released on interim bail for a period of six months on such terms and conditions as the learned trial Court deems it proper, after an affidavit is filed by the petitioner and his mother that they will accept the victim as wife of the petitioner,
including the following conditions:-
(i) He shall not indulge in any criminal activity while on bail.
(ii) He shall not try to tamper with evidence or influence prosecution witnesses while on bail.
(iii) He will remain present in the trial Court on each date it is fixed for trial.
(v) He shall surrender before the learned trial court.
immediately after expiry of the interim bail of six months.
10. Violation of any condition will entail in cancellation of the interim bail.
11.
The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
